questions.stem: A 32-bit application must run on a new 64-bit Windows workstation. Is this possible?

choices.text: No - 64-bit OS cannot run 32-bit apps
Yes - 64-bit OS runs both 32-bit and 64-bit apps
Only if the app is reinstalled with a 64-bit installer
Only on Windows 10, not Windows 11

questions.explanation: A 64-bit OS can run both 32-bit and 64-bit applications. 32-bit apps on a 64-bit Windows are stored in Program Files (x86).
questions.trap: (a) reverses the rule. Only a 32-bit OS is restricted - it cannot run 64-bit apps.

questions.stem: A technician installs a 64-bit OS on a workstation. Which type of hardware driver must be installed for the NIC?

choices.text: 32-bit driver, as it is backward compatible
64-bit driver, to match the OS architecture
Either 32-bit or 64-bit - drivers are universal
The OS installs the correct driver automatically

questions.explanation: Drivers must match the OS architecture. A 64-bit OS requires 64-bit drivers. 32-bit drivers are not compatible.
questions.trap: (a) Drivers are not backward compatible across architectures. (d) Auto driver detection doesn't guarantee the right bitness.

questions.stem: A user needs to run 3D CAD modeling software. The integrated graphics in their laptop are not supported by the application. What is the solution?

choices.text: Upgrade to a 64-bit OS
Add more RAM
Install a discrete (dedicated) graphics card
Increase the paging file size

questions.explanation: Integrated graphics are built into the CPU and insufficient for demanding 3D applications. A discrete graphics card provides the separate GPU power required.
questions.trap: Adding RAM or paging file won't fix a graphics shortfall. 64-bit OS has no bearing on GPU capability.

questions.stem: A high-end engineering application will not launch unless a specific USB device is connected to the computer. What type of licensing is this?

choices.text: Subscription license
Volume license
Hardware token (dongle)
OEM license

questions.explanation: A hardware token (dongle) is a physical USB device the application checks for at launch. Without it, the software will not run. Common for expensive professional applications.
questions.trap: Subscription and volume licenses are software-only and managed online or with keys, not physical devices.

questions.stem: An IT team needs to deploy the same OS configuration to 200 new identical workstations. What is the most efficient method?

choices.text: Install from the Windows ISO on a USB drive at each workstation
Use an OS image (clone) to deploy the fully configured system
Remote Desktop into each machine and install manually
Use the Windows upgrade assistant

questions.explanation: OS imaging creates one fully configured base image (OS + patches + apps + settings) and deploys it to multiple machines in minutes. Hardware must be identical or use virtual machines.
questions.trap: Manual USB install at each workstation would take hours per machine. Imaging reduces this to minutes with consistent results.

questions.stem: A user installs a new application. The next day, several shared network folders that the user had mapped are showing unexpected changes. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: The network administrator changed the share permissions
The application ran with the user's rights and accessed the shared folders
Windows Update modified the network configuration
The application requires administrator rights to use network shares

questions.explanation: An installed application inherits the logged-in user's rights and permissions, including access to mapped network drives. An untested or malicious app can modify, delete, or read anything the user can.
questions.trap: Many users assume apps are sandboxed. They are not - they run with full user-level access to all resources the user has.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid sources for installing an application? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Download directly from the software manufacturer's website
Install from the OS's official app store
Install from a USB drive in an air-gapped environment
Download from any third-party site for faster access

questions.explanation: Trusted sources include the manufacturer's website, official app stores, and local media. Third-party download sites risk tampered installers containing malware.
questions.trap: (d) Third-party sites are a security risk even if the download looks legitimate. Stick to official sources.
